headline: Semantic Kernel’s broad network/MCP and file access create medium-to-high interaction risks; LlamaFactory is read-only but can still be a prompt source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or file I/O, so direct injection is limited. B can read application-defined files and use MCP/plugins, so if A’s outputs are manually or indirectly fed into B, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is not default, but B’s permissive tool-use surface makes it plausible.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is copied into B’s prompt or a file B reads
IF B’s plugin or MCP parser treats file content as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in B prompts
Require provenance tags on all A-generated content
Restrict B MCP/plugins to allowlisted sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B reads files, writes files, and calls external APIs. If sensitive application context is placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit it to third-party model providers. A is not a leak source, but B’s default surfaces make leakage plausible once shared data exists.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in files or context that B can read
IF B routes that context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of B-readable workspaces
Use a redaction step before B receives context
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Separate credentials from application context
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B can write files and use application-defined files, but without a writable counterpart in A there is no meaningful write-write conflict. The only overlap is read-side interaction, which is not a capability conflict.
conditions: IF A is replaced with a writable agent
IF both agents are given the same mutable directory or git repo
mitigations: Keep A read-only
Assign B a separate workspace
Avoid shared git repositories
Use per-agent file namespaces
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate outputs that B may consume, and B’s plugin/function-calling pattern can act on that context without an explicit verification layer. Because A is not runnable and B is the action-capable component, the main risk is B treating A’s text as authoritative. This is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as input without a validation step
IF B executes tool calls based on A-generated facts or citations
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts
Require B to cite source provenance
Limit B to read-only summarization mode
Flag A outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add policy checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and touches no data classes, while B handles application context and secrets and can send data to external providers. If regulated or residency-bound data flows through B, the compliance burden is on B’s broad API and secret-handling surfaces; A is not the compliance driver. The mismatch is plausible but not specifically documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B’s application context
IF B sends that data to non-approved external providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B workflows
Restrict B to approved providers only
Review retention settings before runs
Separate secrets from user content
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency controls
